question:
A 88-year-old man is evaluated in the emergency department for 4 hours of anterior chest discomfort
that developed after he was moving furniture and then resolved. He describes the pain as a pressure in
the front of his chest, with radiation to the left shoulder. He began intermittent hemodialysis 6 months
ago for end-stage kidney disease attributed to hypertensive nephrosclerosis. He notes lower-extremity
edema that resolves after dialysis but is otherwise asymptomatic. He has had hypertension for more
than 30 years and also has hyperlipidemia. His current medications are aspirin, metoprolol,
simvastatin, losartan, calcium acetate, and erythropoietin. On examination, his blood pressure is
156/91 mm Hg, and his heart rate is 65 beats per minute. At rest, he appears to be comfortable and
without pain. The pain is reproduced when he rotates his body and upon palpation of his anterior chest
on the left side. He has a normal cardiac examination and clear lung fields. Bilateral trace edema is
present. An electrocardiogram indicates left ventricular hypertrophy with repolarization abnormality,
consistent with previous electrocardiographic results. Laboratory testing, conducted before dialysis,
reveals a hemoglobin level of 10.8 g/dL (reference range, 13.5–17.5) and a potassium level of 5.0
mEq/liter (3.5–5.0). A cardiac troponin-T level, obtained in the emergency department upon arrival
using a 4th-generation assay, is 0.2 ng/mL (0–0.03). Which one of the following management
approaches is most appropriate for this patient? Answer Choices: (A) Discharge home with outpatient
follow-up scheduled within 3 days (B) Refer for orthopedic evaluation for musculoskeletal pain (C)
Await a second cardiac troponin-T level for comparison at 4 hours after presentation (D) Repeat the
electrocardiogram every 30 minutes for 2 hours (E) Perform immediate bedside echocardiography (F)
Start a nitroglycerin infusion for suspected acute coronary syndrome (G) Refer for immediate cardiac
catheterization with coronary angiography (H) Initiate high-dose intravenous heparin therapy
immediately (I) Prescribe nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs for chest wall pain (J) Proceed with
emergent dialysis to manage hyperkalemia
 A. Perform immediate bedside echocardiography
B. Discharge home with outpatient follow-up scheduled within 3 days
C. Start a nitroglycerin infusion for suspected acute coronary syndrome
D. Refer for immediate cardiac catheterization with coronary angiography
E. Initiate high-dose intravenous heparin therapy immediately
F. Await a second cardiac troponin-T level for comparison at 4 hours after presentation
G. Repeat the electrocardiogram every 30 minutes for 2 hours
H. Proceed with emergent dialysis to manage hyperkalemia
I. Refer for orthopedic evaluation for musculoskeletal pain
J. Prescribe nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs for chest wall pain
